findings.passage: “From day one, many individuals dismissed our work as a ‘witch hunt’—but the facts speak for themselves: non-citizen voting is real here in our state, and even one illegal ballot undermines the trust we are told to have in our election processes and even the Republic itself,” said Attorney General Rokita.
findings.note: Release announcing a settlement with the federal Department of Homeland Security that upgrades its SAVE citizenship-check tool for all states. Claims at least 165 non-citizens registered and 21 voted in Indiana, based on preliminary federal results. Date taken from the page's listed start date.

findings.passage: “This case shows exactly why we need the SAVE America Act and why Congress should act immediately to pass this common-sense legislation,” Attorney General Rokita said. “If a simple checkbox is enough for an illegal alien to register and vote in election after election, then others could easily do so as well, and many have across the country. If it’s happening in a state like ours, which has strong photo ID laws, imagine how rampant it is in a state like California, where basically nothing is done to safeguard its elections.”
findings.note: Release on felony charges against a man alleged to have registered and voted as a non-citizen. He calls for the SAVE America Act, which the release says would require documentary proof of citizenship such as a birth certificate or passport to register for federal elections.

findings.passage: “This critically important prosecution is just another step in the work I’ve been doing ever since I was Secretary of State, when I led the effort that made Indiana the first state in the nation to enact a photo voter ID law.  It is part of our office’s and the Secretary of State’s office’s ongoing efforts to ensure our elections are safeguarded and sends a clear message that voting by noncitizens will not be tolerated.”
findings.note: Same release. He ties the prosecution to his earlier work on Indiana's photo voter ID law. The release also says Indiana recently passed its own proof-of-citizenship law, which is in litigation, and that he has defended it successfully so far.
